rounds.text: Despite headline growth figures, A.K.Capital Services Ltd suffers from a severe cash flow crisis, evidenced by a negative operating cash flow and free cash flow of Rs -171 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. This poor cash generation results in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -2.76x against reported profit, with operating cash flow at -127% of operating profit [E30, E33]. Compounding these liquidity concerns, working capital requirements have deteriorated drastically, with working capital days surging from 187 days to 523 days [E57]. The underlying return profile also remains weak over medium-term horizons, highlighted by a low median return on equity of just 7% over 10 years, 8% over 5 years, and 8.51% over the last 3 years [E26, E27, E56]. Furthermore, the stock's valuation disconnects from its capital efficiency, as reflected by a higher EV/EBITDA of 10.37x compared to the sector benchmark of 3.14x and a subpar ROCE of 9.43% against a sector benchmark of 47.42% [E10, E11]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing profit growth and a discounted cash flow suggesting upside [E21, E38].
